text:
Missed entry on EUR/GBP and AUD/JPY.

I was driving in a traffic jam when this happened. Should've removed the orders since the trade happened already, but safety is of #1 priority during driving and fiddling with gadgets/phone is the surest path to accidents and possible death scenario, so I closed the platform.

EUR/GBP then went to TG1 as previously analyzed and a bit more after the missed entry. Triggered the previous missed order and stopped me out.

Entering another position at the CP swap FL directly below as there was a clear demand injection at the base/origin of move up aligned with LS kink.

The AUD/JPY trade is then triggered close to home and it is still currently open in profit.

Lesson from this is definitely clear:Cancel open orders if it is missed because of spread widening USD/CAD was also triggered last night and still open.

Added two more pairs to watch and they are non-correlated with each of the other four pairs.

So my current study list are: AUD/JPY, EUR/GBP, USD/CAD, NZD/CHF, NOK/SEK, Gold.

Hopefully that would take care of the correlation risk issue since I am choosing one of each currency The reason for this is not due to greed and fear of missing out moves. Using HTF charts, imho, slows down the analysis time required so I still can follow the market more efficiently during day job non-hectic times. But watching HTF needs more patience because we have to wait for price to move a larger amount of pips to engulf and create FLs. Watching LTF is definitely impossible during my work hours. Usually too exhausted at night and proper rest is required for the next day.

author: Frosty
text:
A weird homework that I am currently doing. Surely the answer to this phenomena lies in the concept of FLs being created and destroyed. This, for me, is the easiest way to spot FO levels and nice places to look for bounces.

I understand they are what we call LS levels. What I look for is price levels that was touched from above and below, preferably to the pip touches. Say we are going from down to up, price would break the SR up, dip, make a decision, then engulf local high (confirming the FTR) which eventually engulfs previous swing's high.

The decision point at the dip after the break of SR is tradeable on return. Preferably with CP, CPLQ, BSZ, or fake SD level approach.

The bounce could happen anywhere inside the FTR, most likely at the SR first, creating liquidity pools below them for ITs to enter at MPL as usual.

The entry would be clear using LTF analysis. Stops are always beyond the FL/FTR in the same scale.

Targets would be the next higher up FO SR (where tricks were played).

Also the usual disclaimer: I don't expect them to workall the time. The ones that fail would be learning opportunities Apologies if this post is a little weird. I want to record everything that might produce green pips

author: Frosty
text:
Disclaimer: This is my personal way of interpreting RTM materials. It could be not what RTM is teaching, but I am currently focusing my research on this recipe. I love the simplicity of this setup. Simple not because it is easy. Simple because I actually understand the exact manipulation that has been done. It is all about decisions in price.

QMs work because it is a major loss for the ITs if they don't take price back to that QM level.

This is what I can quickly see when opening up charts now, after many hours of studying RTM materials.

Bro master Salivan gave out the first major clue. It was something along the lines of: read the orders, not rectangles.

Bro Staurum gave out the second major clue. It was approximately: retailers are fanatical about to-the-pip SR levels.

The hint from bro Staurum was an eye-opener. It is summed up in Master IF's quote: Look for tricks being played into places where tricks were played in the past.

The trick that I focused on here is the RS "validation" trick. Please see the charts for explanations It's jaw-dropping how RTM material works in ALL MARKETS.

First up, USD/IDR chart (Note: IDR stands for Indonesian Rupiah). Now I know the best price levels to buy Next chart, USD/PLN chart (Sis Ysbail's currency if I'm not mistaken)

The current difficulty though is about the targets. This, quite understandably, needs full understanding of scales.

I understand that the targets are also places where retailers are trapped as well, but from the other side of the trade.

author: Frosty
text:
Hi all, Although it is still early, I want to wish you all a joyful Christmas and New Year Currently, the office that I work in looks like a graveyard at 2 A. M. in the morning.

Almost everyone except two in my department took early Christmas and New Year’s leave already.

Just the perfect time and place to do some major thinking and mind- dumping again in this journal.

Psychological Stuff: I have learned some important psychological things (out of so many others) throughout my journey in RTM this year. For some, this is the same common sense reiterated stuff, but I will put this here anyway, mostly for my personal reminder: 1. Be in a really, really positive mindset when trying to learn new materials. A happy mind would process new information a lot faster than a grumpy, stressed mind. Try it to believe it. A trick that I personally use is to play a favorite song in low volume in the background for a bit before starting to study. 2. Compare yourself not with others, but with your past self. The you today should be better than the you yesterday. The you tomorrow should be better than the you today. Comparing yourself with other people is like comparing apples to kiwis or mangoes. Even if they are in the fruits category, they will never ever be the same.

3. Give yourself time to process new information and believe that you are improving with time, both on and off the charts. The on/off ratio is different for everyone, I guess. For me personally, it is more like 40% on / 60% off ratio. I didn’t believe this at first, but gave it a try and some concepts that I didn’t understand before seems a lot easier to understand the second time around.

4. Trading is a discipline that needs to be enforced by ourselves. It’s a lot different than working in a corporate environment where our boundaries, rules and job description are given to us right from the start. I believe it is why not many people succeed in trading. They fail to set rules and boundaries. 5. Connected to point 4 above, in my opinion and from my observations of masters and successful traders here, trading requires a super focusing ability and extra detail-oriented mind. It is amazing to be amongst people who asked whether 0.1 – 0.3 pip break of FL is an engulf or not. 6. Think again about concepts that you think you already knew inside out. If there are new questions that pop out, then further investigation is necessary. Do not ignore this because, imho, these questions come from your intuitive mind (not from the logical left side of the brain).

Technical Matters: Today is analyzing flags and FLs time. Without additional words from me here are the important posts that I found across RTM.

Engulf and FO: Engulf and FO. Why the immediate closer UFL didn't hold.

This issue confused me for a while and bro Gregg gave a definite answer there.

After engulf, I would be TT-ing all possible places that price could potentially turn price. This consumed my confidence as price most of the time blast through without any reaction in many of the places that I marked.

PA is the answer, unless trading has become instinctive like master traders here, then we can TT with conservative targets.

When can we know a retracement is complete: Retracement answer I understood this from Lite video #1. Should be no surprise to everyone. If target for engulf is reached, we can then draw the previous FL. Otherwise price would still be in expanding flag.

The above should already be easy for everyone here, now today I saw a chart by bro VitalDrughere.

Side note: Post 212 – 218 in bro VD’s journal is a must read, imho.

My mind instantly switched to Master IF’s drawing from his journal.

Which then related the above diagram and bro VD’s chart to this diagram by Master Staurum.

I trust my mind is trying to tell me something here because the diagrams come in an instant to mind without logically thinking.

Now I’ve been thinking about this diagram and what I can conclude for now, that makes sense out of most of the things said about FLs, scales and MPLs, is that the purple box that I added in the diagram is the FL for an even higher TF.

So scenario X engulfing the red UFL would cause a retrace to Y since the red UFL is the last clean set of orders in the even higher TF Flag.

I failed to notice that Y is not an engulf Engulf this HTF FL, even without breaking the even higher TF FL is a signal to go higher in the future (Master Salivan’s FOF article). Then we would most likely take the last clean orders on the other side from this scale to the direction of the engulf, which is north in this case.

Did that make sense or am I confusing myself again? Thank you all for your continued guidance and hints

author: Frosty
text:
Hi bro Bill and bro AK, Thank you for this awesome discussion My previous line of thinking is similar to bro AK’s and this diagram puzzles me a lot since its inception.

After engulf X, previously I would expect FL B to hold because what I understand is that price would need to reach its target first before breaking the source FL. Basically the question was:why did B break? Shouldn’t the source FL of engulf not break?

But, then the FTR/FL diagram really got me thinking about orders that haven’t been picked up on the way up. I think what might be the key here is differentiating which are the true FLs. Please see the modified diagram below.

According to the Litevideo #1, we know that FL A – D are FLs due to the fact that they were defined after reaching their respective targets, but only A and D are the true FLs (in this specific diagram) because price movement picked up the leftover orders in FL A and D, but in FLs B and C, price failed to do so.

So for example in FL B’s case, 1 failed to pick up 2. In FL C’s case, this could be iSR scenario where price failed to reach the target at FL D. in FL D’s case, 3 returned to pick up orders at 4. I’m thinking price would be more inclined to FO past B and C maybe because of this specific“didn’t return to pick up the orders”reason.

Walkthrough of my understanding of the price movement process: 1. Break of blue FL down, immediate target is FL B. EDIT: the next immediate target is next LFL not shown here, but there is a high chance of price filling down to FL B (just to avoid confusion) 2. At B, ITs would make a decision to break B or to bounce from B.

Decision is needed because price has reached its target. We would need to look for PA again at Z.

3. In either case, price would be attracted to (but not guaranteed) the true FL at D, specifically its MPL, because B and C are weaker levels due to the fact they failed to return to pick up the orders. 4. When price reaches FL B and C, we would look for PA also for possible bounces. Bounces would probably be smaller amount due to the fact that they are midrange relative to the move from D to A.

What I’m very certain of is only point 1 and 2 in the above walkthrough. What happens after the engulf X is still a mystery to me and if we can solve this, I think we are better equipped to imagine price movement scenarios.

Looking forward to hear your thoughts on this matter. Hopefully our friends who have this figured out already could give us a hint in the right direction. I apologize if I’m confusing anyone.

Likewise, after C is created, price went to hit FL 2, so then C becomes an FL too.
